headline: McMaster authors report agent-led topology and layout of a nanowatt biomedical filter
fact: McMaster University authors report an LLM-agent workflow that moved a fourth-order, 250-Hz biopotential low-pass filter from topology exploration through schematic and layout iterations on IHP SG13G2. The agents combined current-reuse techniques, tested candidates in simulation and produced a DRC- and LVS-clean layout. The paper reports nominal post-extraction simulation meeting its specification, with 41.6% lower input-referred noise than its reference at about equal core power. A human approved the specification and layout plan. These are reported simulation results, not measured silicon or unqualified autonomous sign-off.

sources.title: Multi-Agent AI Design of a Nanowatt Biomedical Low-Pass Filter from Topology to Layout — arXiv record
sources.summary: The arXiv record gives the October 19, 2026 v1 submission, McMaster authors and the reported filter and post-layout simulation results. It states that the manuscript was submitted to ISCAS 2027, not accepted.

sources.title: Multi-Agent AI Design of a Nanowatt Biomedical Low-Pass Filter — full manuscript
sources.summary: The full manuscript details topology A/B tests, human approvals, agent review, DRC/LVS and nominal post-extraction simulation; it distinguishes its simulated filter from measured designs in the comparison table.
